If sentiment is >0.5 in the last 3 days and forecast is rising, reduce late-period forecast by 1.5–2.5% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is <0.5 and forecast is falling, increase mid-period forecast by 1.0–1.5% to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.0 after a downward trend, shift forecast peak earlier by 2–3 days and reduce late-period volatility.  
If sentiment is consistently low (0.0–0.3) and forecast is flat, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in early period to avoid underestimating rebound.  
If sentiment is high (0.7–1.0) and forecast is rising, cap late-period growth at 1.0% above mid-period to prevent runaway inflation.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, smooth transition by averaging adjacent forecast points and reduce amplitude by 20–30%.
